identity.title: ZFYVE21 is an essential host factor for influenza A virus by regulating endosomal acidification.

content.abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) remains a major global health threat, causing recurrent seasonal epidemics and sporadic pandemics. Despite extensive studies on IAV-host interactions, cellular regulation of the viral life cycle is not fully understood. Here, using genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screens, we identified zinc finger FYVE domain-containing protein 21 (ZFYVE21) as a cellular factor required for completion of the IAV life cycle. We show that ZFYVE21 acts upstream of PTEN to maintain endosomal acidification, which triggers the conformational change of viral hemagglutinin (HA) required for membrane fusion and viral uncoating. Deficiency of ZFYVE21 abrogates this acidification step, thereby blocking viral genome release into the cytosol and subsequent replication across multiple IAV strains. Importantly, ZFYVE21-deficient mice exhibit significantly lower lung viral loads, diminished histopathological damage, and markedly improved survival upon lethal IAV H3N2 challenge. Collectively, our findings uncover a critical role of ZFYVE21 in endosomal acidification-dependent IAV genome release into the cytosol and establish ZFYVE21 as a promising target for the development of broad-spectrum anti-influenza therapeutics.
